findings.failure_path: Owner evidence is only recorded when the skill tool call supplies `args.name` (slug-shaped) and the result supplies `metadata.name`/`metadata.dir`. The prior `safeTranscriptInput` path that recorded `args.skill` was deleted. On any OpenCode build whose skill tool uses a different argument key or omits `metadata.dir` (the retained evidence covers exactly one local 1.18.15 build), `completedSkill` returns null for every load and every subsequent `task` dispatch is rejected with a delegation-owner guard error, with no diagnostic distinguishing 'unowned skill' from 'unsupported host shape'. The diff's own `old-shape` and `missing-name` cases encode this total block as expected behavior, so no test would catch the version-compatibility break.
findings.smallest_fix: When `tool === "skill"` and neither the recognized `args.name` nor `metadata.dir` shape is present, emit a distinct explicit unsupported-host-shape error/notice from the guard instead of silently producing no owner evidence.

findings.failure_path: OpenCode asset installation is now conditional on `command -v opencode`. Without `--with-agent-skills`, a host that has OpenCode installed but not on the invoking shell's PATH (GUI/AppImage install, non-login shell, CI prepopulating ~/.config/opencode) takes the else branch, runs nothing, and the script still reaches the final `note "完成。重启 ..."` banner with exit 0. The user is told installation completed while no skills, plugin, commands, bootstrap, runtime or manifest were written. test_unified_skips_absent_opencode_without_creating_config asserts exactly this exit 0 no-op, so the overclaim is locked in by the test.
findings.smallest_fix: When the opencode CLI is not detected and no assets were installed, print the skip on stderr and suppress the completion banner (or still install to ~/.config/opencode, which the CLI reads regardless of PATH).

findings.failure_path: `spawnSync` timeout + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` signals only the immediate child. A host launcher that is a shell/node wrapper spawning a real CLI without `exec` leaves the grandchild alive holding the inherited stdout/stderr pipes, so the synchronous read does not reach EOF and the call can block well past HOST_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS — defeating the stated 'must not hold up other hosts' guarantee. The timing assertion in host-probe-timeout.test.mjs uses a single direct child that is itself killed, so it passes regardless.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` with a detached process group and kill the group on timeout, or add a fixture whose fake CLI forks a surviving grandchild and assert the elapsed bound.

findings.failure_path: `preflight` drift is now fatal for install and update (`code 3, status "collision"`) and for doctor (`shared-drift`). A single user-created file inside an owned `skills/<name>` directory — or a mode change on one owned file — makes every subsequent update permanently impossible; the reported drift entry for the directory case is just `skills/<name>`, which does not name the offending extra file. There is no force/repair/re-adopt path in the diff, so the only recovery is manual guessing at which file to delete.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the specific unexpected/missing file paths in the drift entry for the skill-directory case so the user can act on the message.

findings.failure_path: The host-failure return was moved ahead of the `!manifest && !current.plugin && !current.marketplace` absent check. On a machine with no Claude CLI and nothing installed, `uninstall` now returns code 4 with 'refusing to drop ownership evidence while registration cannot be verified' instead of the previous `0/absent`. In aggregate `uninstall`, `owned()` only tests directory existence, so a leftover empty `~/.claude/ccl-skills-npm` with no manifest selects the host and turns a genuine no-op into a nonzero multi-host-partial result.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep the host-failure return but short-circuit to `0/absent` first when there is no manifest and no owned root content.

concern_results.conclusion: Counterexamples found. (1) Native skill provenance is now derived exclusively from OpenCode's `args.name` + `output.metadata.{name,dir}` shape; the previous `args.skill` transcript fallback was deleted, so any host version using a different skill-tool arg/metadata shape produces no owner evidence and permanently rejects every task dispatch (the diff's own "old-shape" case asserts rejection). The retained evidence explicitly states the shape was read from one local OpenCode build. (2) install.sh now gates all OpenCode asset installation on `command -v opencode`, so the default invocation on a host where the CLI is not on PATH does nothing and still prints the success banner with exit 0. (3) Claude uninstall's host check was moved ahead of the absent check, converting a genuine no-op uninstall into code 4. (4) OpenCode drift is now fatal for doctor/install/update with no repair path. Registration absence is not inferred from an unavailable host anywhere in the diff, and ownership is not inferred from filename prefixes; the `ccl-*.md` prefix delete in sync_commands was in fact removed, which is a separate behavior change (stale package commands are no longer pruned) not covered by any test in this diff.

Filesystem boundaries hold: `assertExclusiveRoot` now covers `snapshots`, `assertSafeSharedParents` runs over old entries before any delete, and the installer's `.pending` backup keeps the first original plus failure-period user additions. The weak boundary is process containment in the new probe: `spawnSync` with `timeout`/`killSignal: SIGKILL` kills only the direct child, so a wrapper that forks and does not exec leaves a grandchild holding the inherited stdout/stderr pipes; the timeout tests only exercise a direct child, so the claimed 10s bound is unverified for the wrapper case. Gate-fireability: the delegation-owner gate cannot be reached without a completed native skill load bound to the active runtime directory, and the gated party cannot self-adjudicate — the caller's `args` alone are never sufficient. No force/re-adopt bypass was added.

challenge_focus: Adversarially challenge host mutation authority, partial registration and update failures, cancellation and unavailable observations, native skill provenance, and recovery preservation. Independently verify any prior findings against actual CLI/source contracts and test controls; do not infer registration absence from an unavailable host or ownership from a filename prefix.
